utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, Mr. Tieger, Miss Hollis, who will call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour. Thank you. The next witness is Sakib Sivac.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before you call the next witness, Judge Stephen would like to raise something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It relates to the last witness or was he the second last, I think, Ermin Strikovic. This may be simply typographical, I do not know, but I see on the names of witnesses that he is said to be involved with counts 1 and 15 to 17. 15 to 17 deals with somebody called, amongst others, Sejad Sivac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: All through the transcript where reference is made to a Sivac, he is shown as S-E-A-D Sivac, whereas in the indictment it is S-E-J-A-D. Is that said to be the same person?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I believe it is a matter of how you write the name because if it is written as it would, perhaps, be pronounced, the J is often pronounced as a Y, so Sead or S-E-A-D without the J. It is meant to be the same person, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Because I see that he was asked, "Again the first name of your friend was what?" and he repeats it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: But it is shown as S-E-A-D.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is a matter of how it is written, I believe. Different people write those names in different ways. We meant it to be the same person. He is speaking of Sejad Sivac, the veterinarian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, have you anything to say about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was something I understood to be the case, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call Mr. Sivac? MR. SAKIB SIVAC called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take the oath that is being handed to you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, will you state your name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sakib Sivac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st March 1959.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Sivci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you attend school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First four grades of elementary school in Trnopolje and the other four in Kozarac, in Rade Kondic school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After finishing school, did you take a course to become a brick mason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1978 did you serve with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following your service with the JNA, did you work for approximately two years in Slovenia and did you later work for about a year with a firm that had work in Bosanski Novi and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those periods of time you were working in those areas, did you come home regularly on weekends to Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in 1985 did you suffer a work related accident and retire as a result?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, with the exception of a few months working in Europe, were you essentially continuously in Sivci until 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as a result of your retirement, did you spend a great deal of time in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the time, almost all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the main shopping area and cafe area for the people of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for us, for me and my village, yes, it was the principal area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have known him since I attended school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the two of you friends or people who knew each other by sight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Friends, no, by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any particular reason why he might have been better known to you than other people who were familiar to you in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning because of karate and then he had a coffee bar, like many other people who were slightly better known in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you and Mr. Tadic passed each other in the street, would you acknowledge each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we would nod.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a common occurrence for you to see him in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any personal dealings with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, once my brother was to work for him, one had to go for -- to bring along some carpentry items, one had to go to Ljubljana and later and I was there when they were discussing it, but it did not get the deal and they did not go. Then my brother asked for his work book and he returned him and then he asked for it, and then he went with his employment book to the company that he used to work before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see Dule Tadic with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see him ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many times he often wore a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see him without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that without a beard and with a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with his appearance both with and without a beard then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, were you in Sivci when the attack on Kozarac began on May 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Sivci.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this map be marked for identification as Exhibit 281 for identification, please? We also have three copies for the Court. Mr. Sivac, do you recognise that map as depicting ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- the area of Sivci in relationship to Kozarac and Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 281 for admission and ask that it be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 281 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we first pan back a bit and show as much of the entire area as we can? Thank you. First of all, Mr. Sivac, can you point to where Kozarac is located on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarac is here. Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to where Trnopolje is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trnopolje is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us now where Sivci is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where Sivci is, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, can you show us where the hamlet of Jaskici was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jaskici is to the right of Sivci here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honour, I would like to have this map or diagram marked as Exhibit 282 for identification, please? Mr. Sivac, do you recognise this as a diagram or map which you put together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that of the Sivci area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. This is the area covering all buildings in Sivci.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 282.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 282 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May 282 be placed on the screen, please? Mr. Sivac, did you make this map or diagram from memory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a computer used to help make it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was explaining to my brother's son. He was working on the computer and he was moving it up and down. I was drawing and then he fed it into the computer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the one with the computer skills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he likes doing that. He is young.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this map intended to be perfectly to scale or roughly to scale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps not 100 per cent, but it is -- all of it is as it is there, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Is it possible that a couple of houses which were located there might not be shown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that all the houses are here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the bottom left of the diagram ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- is that an area of tiny houses or did you run out of room at the bottom of the page and have to cram it together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was no room simply there, identical houses as those ones up there. There were simply no room on this sheet of paper and that is why they are so crammed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the right bottom portion of the map or diagram, that is a portion which was entered by hand rather than with a computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I added this because again it would not fit and this is a continuation of this main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I note that there are numbers on the houses. Were those numbers for the purpose of noting how many houses there were in Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I drew it simply to count them, to see how many there used to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a small river that runs through the area of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was called Jaruga and it is here and it flows here, but this was not drawn. We started drawing and then stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a bit too difficult to put in with the computer because of the bends and twists of the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, if I could just ask you about a couple of locations on this map? First of all, can you show us where your home was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] This is my house. 17, I think it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have family living in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that include your father and brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my father was across the way here and my brother and I was alone here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us which is your father's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] This here under 71.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother's home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is one, 70, 72, 72 and 73.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Thank you. Did your youngest brother live at home with your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my youngest brother stayed to live with father. It was his home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the attack on Kozarac began on May 24th, were you able to hear or see the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could hear it very well and one could also see up the hills above the Prijedor/Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How intensive was the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning it was continuous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what areas did it appear to be concentrated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shells were mostly falling on the part of Kozarac, Kozarusa, Jakovici, Brdjani. Some would also go astray and fall below the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the "asphalt" you mean the Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which separated the Kozarac area from the area where you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, let me ask you a few questions about the first two or three days following the attack on Kozarac. Were the Muslim people of the Sivci area instructed to surrender weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you were aware, did everyone who had a weapon turn it in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the weapons which were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I, when they were bringing, here, on this road here, this is where they were collecting it. There was a blanket there because there were very few weapons so they put them on the blanket, and they put them in the car and took it away. Osman Sivac and Hase Icic were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did you see? What kind of weapons were collected and how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact number. There were not many. There were hunting rifles, pistols and there was one M48 rifle. That was my neighbour's Nagib Sivac's. This is his home. He was a member of the TO in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, one question I did not ask you, can you tell us the ethnic composition of the inhabitants of the area shown on the diagram you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Sivci?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority, they all were Muslim with the exception of this house here, No. 76. That was not a Muslim house. All the others were Muslim households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the nationality of the person who lived in the home which you have indicated by No. 76? The home you were just talking about, Mr. Sivac, what was the nationality of the person or persons who lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Ukrainian, those who came from Russia, from Ukraine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, during the first two or three days following the attack on Kozarac, did people from Sivci attempt to flee in the direction of Kozarac to the forest during a lull in the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they tried to. The panic started. A column was formed and they tried to head for the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how large was that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column was about a kilometre and a half long, tractor after tractor after tractor, car after car after car -- very many women, children, men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the column reach the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not. We reached in the village of Dergici, which is above Sivci, and we stopped by the home of one Saban Dergic at the cross-road because the shells were beginning to hit Dergici as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After seeking shelter for a period of time, did the people who had attempted to flee in the column return to their homes in Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed up there. People ran for some shelter into bushes, into a thicket. We stayed there for about two or three hours and then we all turned back to Sivci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first two or three days following the attack, did refugees from the area of Kozarac flee to Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we returned the same day but large groups of refugees began to arrive the next day and the day after that. They talked about very many dead in Kozarac and Jakovici and they were all frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many refugees from the area of Kozarac would you estimate fled to Sivci at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot claim with any certainty, but there were about 4,000 to 5,000 people in Sivci then, all the houses, all the garages, all the barns, everything was full, all the stables. I had 45 refugees in my home and we were 50 altogether with my wife and children, and in my old man's home, in my father's and other homes where the houses were larger, there were up to 100 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, were the men from the Sivci area eventually rounded up and taken to camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were caught on 14th June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the attack on Kozarac and 14th June, were Muslim men from Sivci taken by Serb forces to collect bodies in the area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Once a Serb soldier Zuna Radivojac came and ordered me to find as many pairs of gloves as possible, and he assigned a group of guys to load the dead with him in Jakovici so he returned with a truck, and Hitko Foric told me they had loaded a number of bodies in decaying state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that same period of time between the attack on Kozarac and the cleansing of Sivci on June 14th, was there shelling of the area or coming from the area of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. During the period of time between the attack on Kozarac and the cleansing of Sivci, was there any shelling of the Sivci area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere at the beginning of June, on 1st or 2nd, somewhere around from my house there is a forest. You could hear the tanks and you could clearly hear the sound of the engines, and there was shelling and people jumped and started -- ran for shelter. The children were screaming and it was horrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the shells land near your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on the house, but it fell between my house and the house of my relative, in between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later see the tanks which had, apparently, been firing coming down the main road through the Sivci area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then I left my house and went to the main road to see how my family is. We were in the yard, maybe 50, up to 100 of us, a lot had hidden in the houses, and two tanks came through very fast, a lot of people on the tanks, raised three fingers and they went very fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time before the cleansing, were the people of Sivci ordered to stay within a certain area or forbidden to go to certain areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the movement was limited. That Zuna Radivojac was often in Sivci and said, "Whoever crosses the asphalt is going to be killed". Some people crossed it and they never came back. They went for food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time did Serb forces come looking for particular individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, often they were looking for someone. I know two cases when people came to, when people showed up in the camps by themselves because they said that if they did not show up that they would shell Sivci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any burning of homes or barns during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was one night, maybe around 10th June, maybe earlier, I do not remember, they were burning houses and barns. The cows and horses were on fire and the cows were moo-ing, and it was horrible. The house next to me burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, what was it like at night for the people of Sivci during this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nights were the worst because Trnopolje was close and there was shooting then at night. We had to sleep dressed and we had very little food. There were people, two or three people, walking around the house so that the house would not be torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did people sleep dressed or why were they in their clothes at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of fear, that we thought that they might be coming. We expected them to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On June 14th, where were you that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On June 14th I was at home with my wife and my wife's mother and brother and my two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that there had been approximately 45 refugees at your home. Were they still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, a day before that they went to the village Mujkanovici. They found an open house and then the men were taken to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned your wife's brother. Had he just come to your home from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he came from Omarska camp. He was too young. At that time they were releasing the young ones. So my wife brought him over to come and to get a bath and he was already -- he had already lost weight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come directly from Omarska camp ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think that the interpreter who is speaking in Serbo-Croat is speaking on Channel 4 because I am hearing you. Go ahead, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your wife's brother, at the time he came to your home, had he just come from Trnopolje camp or Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the previous days had she been attempting to get him food at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day had she managed to get permission to bring him to your home for that day in order to get him bathed and give him some food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she managed to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were in your home with the family members you mentioned, did you hear the sound of shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that day the shooting started around 10 o'clock in the morning, and the shooting was approaching. It was coming closer and closer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Serb forces come to your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they come into your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was sitting at home. I was drinking coffee, and suddenly I think somebody kicked in the door, and he walked in with an automatic rifle and asked who was the owner of the house and I said that it was myself. This soldier -- it was a soldier -- he ordered me to take him upstairs, walk in front of him, see if there are other men in the house. We went upstairs to the top floor. We saw that there was nobody there. He checked it. Then he made me lead him downstairs again and then we went down to the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came downstairs were other Serb soldiers or members of Serb forces there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I came downstairs to the hallway two Serb soldiers were standing in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you came downstairs? Did they say anything to you or do anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the two who were standing tried to hit me and the one who was behind him who held a rifle told him not to touch me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they order you outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they told me to get out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or any member of your family ask what was going to be done with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My wife came out and asked where they were taking me, and the one with a beard who was there who led me out of the house said that we had to walk in front of the tanks because the green berets are shooting, and that we had to lead the column of tanks and then we would come back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they told you you were to be used as a shield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they said that we had to walk in front of the tanks and then he said -- my wife said that I did not have any weapons, that nobody was shooting. He said that, told her to shut up, that she did not know where she was living and who she was living with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, once you were outside did the Serb soldiers ask you where other Muslims could be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that one behind me with a beard, he asked me several times about the houses of my two neighbours' houses, Osman Sivac and Munib Sivac, and I sort of showed them to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Outside did you see your neighbours in the area of the lane or road on which your house is which leads to the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw across from my neighbours this house here. [The witness indicated on the plan] There were these young men from Jakupovici. There were about 10 or 11 of them. They were made to walk in front and they were beating them to walk to the road, and then when we came out they asked me to join them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, I think when you were indicating the area of your house and the direction in which those men were walking, the map was not on the screen. I am going to ask to have that put on the screen so you can indicate that area again. If you will wait just a moment? If you could point that out again, sir, the area where your house is located and the direction in which those neighbours were going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] This is my house here and the one across is my neighbour's house, and here they drove out about 10, 11 young men. He had four sons. They were beating them and they were hurting them, and it is a small distance between these two houses and then they said to stand there with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you and the other people from the area immediately around your house directed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were standing there and then suddenly there was an order "Hands behind your backs", and I ran down towards the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We ran along this road straight towards the main road, and as we ran, as parallel to the bridge here there was a tank and we came to stop here in front of this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you directed to hold your hands as you were running?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Always behind the head like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see other Serb forces coming toward the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them in the fields. They were always in two's and three's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Serb forces on the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, around the tank always, and there were a lot of them, a lot of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they firing any weapons or was the tank firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A man on the tank had some big machine gun and he shot some and then the rest of the soldiers were shooting constantly and cursing, "Catch them alive". We who were in the yard here, we were just being herded there and beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there for about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other groups of Muslims coming down the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment a group ran by along the main road in the direction of Trnopolje and then they told us, "OK, run down the road and hold your hands behind your heads", and then at one point an order came, "Lie down". Then as we ran we had to lie down, and then we would run for another few metres and then lie down again. Then they would beat us and kick us again. They were pulling out wallets, IDs, money and then they were throwing it away. As we kept running down, there were more and more documents on the roadway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the group eventually end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the end the group arrived in the yard of Hamid Sivac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far away from where the path or road to your home meets the main road was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 150, 200 metres from the house where we started, from this house down to about this one here, about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Could you ask the witness to point again?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sivac, can you point to the house of Hamid Sivac where you stopped and tell us the number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] This is the house of Hamid Sivac. It is marked as house 27.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how many times would you estimate you and the others in your group were forced to lie down and then get up again as you proceeded towards Hamid Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Myself and the group that was with me, maybe 20, 30 of us, I think, had to get down on the ground at least 30, 40 times, lie down, get up, run again, lie down and they kept beating us and kicking us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some people having more trouble with this process of lying down and getting up and running and lying down again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were elderly people and there were also people who were heavier, and the ones -- we, who were younger, it was easier on us and it was more difficult on the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the members of the Serb forces do to these people, these older and heavier people, who were having trouble?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also beat them, but they got more than the others, you know, kicks and blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Hamid Sivac's house, in what portion of the house did you stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We entered the yard and the soldiers were around, and they were already commandeering us into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how many Muslims were collected in Hamid Sivac's yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 300, 350 Muslims were there in the yard. There were a few Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of many of the 300 to 350 people who were gathered there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in a bad condition. I think that no one escaped getting something, some kind of a blow. There were a lot of people who were blooded, and one of the Chetniks, the main one, ordered that we should wash ourselves in the well -- there was a well in the yard -- so that those who had blood on them would wash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many Serb forces were at Hamid Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the yard not many, but around a lot, in the fields, behind barns, behind houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show a portion of a video now that I believe the technical people have ready. (The video was shown) Mr. Sivac, do you recognise what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the store in Sivci. This is the road to Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you stop that, please? Can we back it up just a moment? That is fine. The road that the vehicle is moving on now, the road directly ahead, which road is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the road that comes from the direction of Kozarac and going to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we are now moving in the direction of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it goes in the direction of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK, on the main road between Kozarac and Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is not the main road. The main road was paved. It had asphalt. This one is going through the village of Dergici and also ends up in the railroad station of Trnopolje. From the main road, it splits off and it goes through the village of Kararici and ends up in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road which leads to the left goes where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That road leads to the hamlet of Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go forward, please? Mr. Sivac, are we as we proceed in this direction moving toward the area of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my oldest brother's house and then this is the second brother's. This is my father's house, and this is my uncle's house. Here, before this house the road splits off leading to my house. Right here to the right, about 160 metres from the main road, this is where they gathered us in front of this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. So, off to the right of this road your home is approximately 150, 160 metres away, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the main road off to the right past this house, that is where my house was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Can we proceed forward a little bit? Can we stop here, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a bridge that I take when I go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn right then at that little bridge and proceed up approximately 150, 160 metres, that is where your house is, along that path?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you go about 160 metres, you turn right and you are right in front of my house. The road over to the left, that is where the weapons were gathering, were being gathered that we had to turn over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we proceed forward just a little bit, please? Stop. Is this house the closest house to the main road along your street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see in this portion of the video the area where you and the other men were gathered before you were ordered to march toward Hamid Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First from my house, there were 12, 13 of us in front of this yard of this house, and there were already 20 or 30 of us then. We stood there and then when a group ran by, they ordered us to follow them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this house No. 15, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Can we go forward, please? Mr. Sivac, are we now moving in the direction of Hamid Sivac's house where you were stopped and collected with the other 350 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is mekte (sic) in Sivci, this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop here. Thank you. The building shown to the right, Mr. Sivac, what is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is like a mosque, it is mekte. It is where you get your religious education.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were marched in the way you described from the area of your house to Hamid Sivac's house, did you notice whether or not the mekte or mosque was burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at that time it was not burned, only after I left Keraterm and went back home to Sivci, that is when I saw that it had been burned. From Trnopolje, we went with the Serb soldier as an escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then have an opportunity to see the condition of the mekte?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I just glanced inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this next series of photographs marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What will be your Exhibit number for the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The video would be 283 and these photographs would be 284A through E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We have not yet got to house No. 27 on the video, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, while we are waiting, perhaps you can show us on your diagram where that building is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mekte, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first building below No. 15, that is 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honour, I might note at this point I am having a little bit of difficulty with the interpretation. I hear the witness saying "mekteb", I see the interpretation come back as "mekte" which is not a word I understand in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: The word is "mekteb" -- a college or school.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it should be spelled, if that can help? Mr. Sivac, could you spell the word for us, please, for the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could again tell us what the name for that religious building was and spell it, if you can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: M, like Malcolm, E-K-T-E-B, mekteb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Sivac, do you recognise what is depicted in those photographs 284A through E?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the mekteb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the condition it was in when you saw it after you were released from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this burnt remains here, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that 284A through E be tendered and placed on the monitor for the Court's viewing.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 284A through E will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, this shows the inside of the mekteb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another shot of the interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It had two rooms. This was the smaller room which served as a classroom for children, and this is the entrance from the road. It faced this entrance, and this is now mekteb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If we could return to the video then and continue on the path between the area of your home and Hamid Sivac's house where you were finally collected. Can we stop here, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Hamid Sivac's house there, the one to the right, and this is the well where those who were bloody washed themselves. There was a large yard here. That is where we were collected. The army was there on the road, and as we were running they were diverting us into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building shown to the extreme right of the screen behind the well, what is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a barn, his stables and the house was a little bit more to the right. Then there is a small shed, an outbuilding, there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, during the period of time that you and the other 300 to 350 men were waiting, did a van come to the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a truck, I saw a van, a red van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise that van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the van belonged to Hilmija Nukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone inside the van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A soldier was driving it and behind him was one with a mask over his head, only eyes could be seen, and he was pointing at us, at the group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What nationality was Hilmija Nukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time were you waiting there, did members of the Serb forces demand to know where any particular people could be found or asked for other information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were firing above our heads, provoking, enquiring about Zemun people, as they called them. They were looking in yards. They asked about Senad Kenjar and they were shouting, "I will kill you all, I will kill you all, where is he?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone singled out in order to ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, another one from Kamicani, from which Maci Kenjar was, Mehmed Alic, called "Medo", was also singled out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that man beaten? Was Medo beaten in order to get him to tell where Maci could be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that one who was the boss beat him, a tall one, blond with gloves but without the tips of the fingers on. Then Maci said he did not know him and then he first beat him with fists, and then he pulled out his knife and tried going with his knife over his throat, and then he took him behind the house and said, "You'll tell us all, you will squeal". A couple of minutes later Medo ran up to us and he was old bloody on the face and his collar, at the back and all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After a period of time at that collection site at Hamid Sivac's house, did buses arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what direction did they come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The buses arrived from below, from the direction of Trnopolje, and were lining here in the direction of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should indicate that, of course, we cannot see where you are indicating on the video monitor, so we will have to be careful to describe it as well as we can. So buses came from the direction of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the direction of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, as we are looking at the video, the buses would be coming toward us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What portion of the road did they park on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, in the direction in which they were moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be on the other side of the road from where you were gathered in the yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Keraterm I saw five, in Sivci I could not see. I saw three in Sivci, but in Keraterm I saw five, when he said, "Why did you bring 350 people to me? Why did you not kill them all?" It was when we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the last bus in the line parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last bus was parked on the bridge, across the bridge, level with Hamid Sivac's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move the video forward just a bit? Can we stop here, please? On the left side of the screen we can see a road leading to the left. Did that road have a local name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this first bridge, this is a road leading to Hamed Sivac's house. The other one, that is where people had their plots of land so that it led to the fields of Hamed Sivac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could make this a little clearer if we could refer back to the diagram you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This short road leads to Hamed Sivac, and this one leads to Munib Sivac's house, crosses the Jaruga I mentioned and out into the fields where people had their plots of lands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house which is marked No. 49, whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Munib Sivac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just below that on the diagram there are two paths leading off the main road, one short, one longer. The longer path, that is the road leading toward Munib Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shorter path just above it, that is the road with a small bridge that leads to Hamed Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Hamed Sivac's house. It was a road serving one house only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I thought 27 was Hamid Sivac's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was going to clarify. [To the witness]: You spoke of Hamed Sivac's house just now and the bridge and the road leading to Hamed Sivac's house. Is that H-A-M-E-D, Hamed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 49 is H-A-M-E-D and 27 one is H-A-M-E-D and the 49 is H-A-M-I-D. That was the yard where we were collected, where this road is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. I am sorry to do this, but I think it may have been confused so let me try once more. Let me start it this way. You went to the home marked as 27, is that right, that is where you were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the yard, yes, of 27.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that Hamid or Hamed Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hamid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With an "I". The small path we see across the road, that is the path leading toward Hamed Sivac's house with an "E"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Hamed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look back to the video monitor, if we see the house shown in the upper left hand portion of the screen and the fence which borders that house, that path is the path toward Munib Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the lower road towards Munib Sivac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can move forward just a little bit? Stop here. In the left hand portion of the screen, that white object shown just below Munib Sivac's path, is that the bridge leading toward Hamed Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a hedge which separates the two on ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The bridge in the road leading ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Between Munib Sivac's path and the path which runs from the bridge. [To the witness]: Is there a hedge between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on either side of Munib Sivac's house is the fence which we can see near that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then a hedge on the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, after the buses arrived, were the Muslims who were collected there ordered to run to the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you ordered to run, in what fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally running with hands behind our heads, and the first ones from the bridge running up here, those to the bus which was parked in front. I boarded the last bus which was standing here on Hamed Sivac's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you among the group of Muslims who ran to the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at the very end, because I thought that perhaps I could hide or something, but I dared not to go down into the field because there were two, not more than three, behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you ran toward the buses or after the other people had run out ahead of you, did you notice whether or not people had discarded items which had Muslim associations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were many watches with Muslim markings, with the crescent and the star, and amulets and charms which are worn for luck. I had one and I discarded it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, you indicated to us that you ran toward the last bus. Was the rear of that bus approximately in the area of Munib Sivac's path or road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Its rear part was right up to the hedge, between Hamed and Munib Sivac's bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you proceed toward that bus? What path did you take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same from the yard except that those who were coming up had to go to the left and I had to turn slightly to the right, then on to Munib's road and then through the hedge. That is how we came out directly to the buses, to the rear door which was on Hamed Sivac's bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went down the main road and then around the back of the bus down a portion of Munib Sivac's road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until you came to a hole in the hedge where you could go through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far down Munib Sivac's road was that area of hedge where you turned left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not far -- you mean from Hamid Sivac's yard?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is about five metres and that is, you can see it on this picture. This is the bridge and a little below the path and on to Munib Sivac's road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, my question was as you went around the bus and started down Munib Sivac's path, how far down Munib Sivac's road did you have to go to before you were able to turn left into a hole in the hedge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five metres, seven -- not far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you went through that hole in the hedge, were you on Hamed Sivac's path?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had to run up to that place with our hands like this. The bus was already full so they were passing by. We were standing there at the rear door of the bus on Hamed's road. I had already passed through the hedge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated you ran to the area of Munib Sivac's road. After you got through the hedge were you still running?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There we had to slow down, because the bus was moving slowly and there was this hedge so that we slowed down. We ran as far as the hedge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you still have your hands behind your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All the time nonstop our hands had to be above the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you trying to look at the Serb soldiers or were you concerned about looking at Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was afraid, no, I did not and I preferred not to see them at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the group slowed as you approached the bus, the rear entrance of the bus, did you then look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, then I saw it was moving slowly and I saw clearly Dule Tadic and Dragoje Cavic. I did not want really to see them, but it was so slow, the bus was moving slowly, so I raised my head and I looked. Dule was to the right of me and Dragoje Cavic was to the left some 80 centimetres from the bus, and the column had to pass between them, between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you approached the rear entrance of the bus, did you make eye contact with either one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was coming close, they were standing like this with automatic rifles and I was drawing close, I knew Dule but not as well as Cavic. With Cavic I socialised on a number of occasions and he seemed to be embarrassed. He nodded his head in greeting and lowered slightly the barrel of his rifle, and I was walking and I turned. I looked at Cavic, I do not know why, perhaps so that he could help me or something, and then the gentleman pushed me with his rifle to speed me up on my way on to the bus, and I turned and I saw his face in full, all the wrinkles and all. I could not see him better than I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who pushed you after you turned to look directly at Cavic and whose face did you see in full when you turned after you were pushed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see clearly the face of Dule Tadic who was standing to the right of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you board the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, although it was not easy because it was full already, but we had to. We were pushing each other.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the question that you asked the witness was who pushed him after he turned and looked directly at Tadic, and whose face did you see in full when you turned after you were pushed. His response was, "I could see clearly the face of Dule Tadic".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I appreciate that. I will clarify that. Mr. Sivac, you indicated that as you were approaching the bus you looked up and saw Dule Tadic and Dragoje Cavic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then as you got closer you made eye contact with Dragoje Cavic who nodded to you and then lowered his weapon, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you indicated that as you began to board the bus you looked to Cavic and then you were pushed. Who was it that pushed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he push you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see that clearly. I was pushed. I was talking to Cavic who was -- not talking but looking at him, and I was pushed, not too strongly, and I had to continue towards the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you indicated that after you were pushed you turned and looked full face at the person who pushed you, and when you turned and looked who was the person you saw full face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dule Tadic and then we were eye to eye, only there was the length of the rifle. That is how we stood facing one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you boarded the bus, were you able to see outside before the bus left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could still look through the window. I was standing by the door for sometime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people boarded the bus after you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two, one or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time those people were boarding and the period of time before the bus left, were you able to see Dule Tadic and Dragoje Cavic outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could. Yes, I could see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, do you recall what Dule Tadic was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it very well. He had a camouflage uniform, a new one, as far as I could see, a new one. He had an automatic rifle with the folding butt. I used to have one like that, so that is why I recognised it. Then he had a pistol, he had a knife on his left and he did not have a cap. He had -- he may have had it down there, and he, I think, had handcuffs on his belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you used to have a rifle with a folding butt, was that when you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, it is an automatic rifle and that was the most common weapon among the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Dule Tadic was clean shaven or had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard, not a long one. I could see his face clearly. Up to here he had a beard, well, I would not be able to say exactly, of about a month growth, 15 days or a month. It depends on how fast it grows. Not a long one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.30 a.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (11.50 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. Mr. Sivac, when the buses left where did they go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went towards Kozarac, about 200 metres, and then they turned around at my two brothers', then they turned around and then they went back towards Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they eventually stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We passed -- in the beginning I thought that we were, they were taking us to the camp, Trnopolje, but we went past Trnopolje and went to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm were guards or soldiers waiting there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was Zigic Zoran. He prepared a welcome with beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned before that someone said something, one of the guards said something, when your group arrived. What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said, "Why did they bring 350 people here? Why did they not kill them all off? What are they going to do with so many people there?" because Keraterm was already full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the prisoners from your bus and the other buses beaten when they got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we all had to get off. We all had to put up our hands against the bus and Zigic had a knife, it was bloodied. He must have stabbed somebody. Then they were taking everything out, combs and nail clippers, whatever, any small things. Then we were made to go into those rooms. They were looking to see if there was any powder on it, to see if somebody was shooting then, if somebody was limping, they would pull up the cuffs so that they could see if there were any wounds, and all this was being done with beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Keraterm I was 56 days, until the camp was closed, dissolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the general conditions or how would you describe the general conditions in Keraterm during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Terrible conditions. There was hunger. For the first six days I ate nothing and then there was dysentery later. Murders every night, taking out, beatings. Those who were shot and killed with a bullet were happy because he did not go through beatings that would take several days, you know, baseball bats, anything that they would beat them with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much food did you receive after the first five or six days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A small slice of bread, and some sort of soup, I do not know what it was, and when they gave that you had to run 20, 30, if they say, "Throw it away", if you had, and then they would beat you if you did not with rifle butts, with barrels. Sometimes we did not dare go, depending on what group it was waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to use toilet facilities there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a toilet, but for a while, and sometimes they asked, "Who wants to go to the toilet", and the first 10 come out and they get beaten up. Then they stopped the toilets and then there was a barrel. We were 570 in No. 2 and then the stench would be, and then it would leak. It was horrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to move around from room to room and see other prisoners whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would happen occasionally, depending on the shift, on the guards. If they were better ones, sometimes they would let us out, but they would sort of cordon the space with hoses that they had and you did not -- you could not cross it. But that was rarely. We were locked in there for three days at a time. It was so hot, and those who were diabetics died there, some from heat. I was at the end of the room and I could not breathe after a while, so I had to move closer to the door and then I ended up being next to the door in No. 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released from Keraterm camp, were you taken to Trnopolje camp for a short time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they came, the long awaited day, we were waiting for it, and then one day, I think at least 20 buses came. The ones from No. 3, they were not beaten very severely. Everybody, they packed the buses and we who went to Trnopolje we were not beaten. We had to bow our heads and they told us that we were going to Trnopolje. Those two buses that were so packed, they went ahead of us and, I do not know, they did not go there. I do not know where they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Trnopolje camp in a convoy which contained mainly women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went first, when I got to Trnopolje, first I went to Sivci to see if there was any food there, and when I saw that there was nothing there then I waited for a convoy. There was a convoy of five buses with elderly and women and children. I somehow managed to get on that and then went over Vlasic to Travnik. In Kozarac, there were another 15 buses and five trailers and they were filled with women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date that you left Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August 13th, a week before those 250 were to get killed on Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, do you see Dule Tadic in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point him out, please, and tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is dressed in a white jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, what colour jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: My mistake. A green jacket. A green colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. May the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Cross-Examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, you told us that on this day, 14th June, that shooting started at about 10 o'clock in the morning and you knew that forces were approaching Sivci, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said that a Serb soldier came into your house. Can you remember what time that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around 1 o'clock in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in your house with your family at this time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time after the search you were then separated from your family, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eventually, you moved down the village to the place that we have been calling a collection point near Hamid Sivac's house where there were some 300 to 350 Muslim men, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, first I was joined with a group that was across from my house, about 12 of us, and then we ran to the road and we joined in with another group and then we all ran together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What I was interested in was at about what time you got to Hamid Sivac's house and waited there in the yard with those other men.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody thought about looking at a watch. We were being beaten. It was around 1 o'clock, and then we waited there for about 10 minutes and then down, down the road. It was "lie down", "get up", "run". Maybe there was about half an hour, up to one hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between half an hour to one hour it took for you to join the collection point where all the other men had been gathered, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this time you were aware of Serb soldiers being in the village. Were you able to have any idea of numbers, about how many soldiers there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw one tank and many soldiers, from all sides. They were coming through the fields. It was obvious that we were surrounded, that you could not leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those soldiers performing the same task that had happened to you? Were they moving the other men to this collection point at Hamid Sivac's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that area of the collection point, did those soldiers remain guarding you or did they move off and go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were not many of them there in the yard. There was a main one and a few other ones and then they were shooting over our heads. That is the one with the gloves with no fingertips, and he had a radio and the others you could see in the fields or in the barn. They were all over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, presumably, what was happening to you as you were moving to this collection point and being given these orders to go down to the ground and then come up again, was something to put you under their control and in fear of their power, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not just fear. There were so many people were bloodied. There was not a single person who did not get a kick or a rifle butt that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that collection point with the shots being fired over your heads, again that was, presumably, something to make you frightened and fearful of what was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what they thought, but I know that it was bad and terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How long did you stay in that yard, the collection point, before the buses came to the roadside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly, but not that long. Until the buses came from Trnopolje, then they forced us on to the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in the third bus, so the other buses had been loaded before you came to your bus, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I want to object. I think that is not a correct summary of the evidence. I do not remember any testimony about the number of buses lined up. I think the witness said he was in the last bus.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He did say that there were three buses, as I recall the testimony, from Sivci five and when he got to Keraterm, and he was in the third. I do not remember that he testified about how long they were lined up, though, but may be so. I will overrule your objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the third one of the ones that I saw and that was the last bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those buses were lined up along the roadside, I think you told us, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on the right, to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had in your mind that you would have preferred to be towards the end getting on to the buses because you wondered whether there would be an opportunity for you to escape or hide and avoid the detention, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was on my mind. I thought there was a shed there and there were some construction supplies, and then when you got up there, then I looked and I saw that there were military in the field beyond it, and so then I turned around and I joined the group that was going towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The buses arrived, as you have told us, from the direction of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first bus, presumably, took the first group of people, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A part of the entire group, we were all one group, and then they ordered "Hands behind your heads and run", and then we had to run on to the buses through the cordon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the first bus filled first, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally, yes, first the first one, then the second and I went to the last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
