utterances.text: Yes. Would it be right to say that the buses were taking about 100 people each bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe, I know, I know how much a bus fits. I know that a glass broke on one of them. It was impossible how many people. One on top of each other were put.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are ordinary transport buses that would ordinarily have been used to take people between towns and villages, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Autotransport Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These buses were taking far more than their usual load of people, the numbers were far greater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At least double, maybe even more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not a case within these buses of people sitting on seats as you would ordinarily do; these buses were crammed up with people, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people sitting on the floor of the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One on top of the other, on the floor, any which way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To get from the collection point on to the buses was the group just being moved as a whole and then suddenly they would say, "That's enough for the first bus"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what they said, but I know what I did. You cannot put everybody in the same bus. When the first one was filled up, then they would fill up the second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those men were in those buses, how were they able to position themselves? Did they have to look down to the ground? Did they have to keep their heads down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody ran like this, and then you would get on until they said it was enough. I think that is how it was. I know that in my bus I came and it was already full, but you had to get on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these buses load at the rear or the front or the side? Where is the access point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about the other two buses from what I saw from that. I entered by the back door of the last bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that stage, as you have told us, there were only a few people behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to force your way on to the bus, presumably, to try to get in and be part of the load?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would not help me to push, because when they got on, then I got on and I just prayed to God to get on as fast as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bus that you got on to, the third bus, was as full as the other two, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very crowded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Again it would be the same scene of men on top of each other, crammed and no space?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To get on to the Auto Prijedor buses that were there, you told us you go through the rear. What kind of doors were on the rear of the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was like an accordion, you know, it is three segments or four, I do not know. There were not -- they were opening on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, operated by air pressure normally, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I am not an expert. They were just opening and closing by themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are these doors in sections on two sides and they close together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this, they were open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you step on to the bus, do you step on to a step and then on to another step to get on to the level where the seats are, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had got on to that bus, did the door shut behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but with difficulty. It was hard. We had to pack more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had stepped up and then you had to use your body to try to get further into the bus so that the other two or three behind you could also step on behind you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you standing or sitting when you got into the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first I stood up, then there was room, there was room where the conductor sat. Nobody, or for some reason nobody used that. Then after the bus started I went over there. I climbed over there and then a lot of other people leaned into that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when the bus moved off you were sitting in that position where the conductor would sit, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not right away. We went up to Sivci and then when we were coming back, that is when I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after your journey had started, you moved to this new position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the buses turned around and started towards Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned when you gave your evidence this morning that the bus appeared to be moving slowly when you were getting on it. You had to step on to this bus that was moving slowly, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not mention that. We were moving slowly. The bus was standing, so stationary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the bus was stationary, you moved slowly and eventually got on and then the doors were shut behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then did the bus move on once the last person had got on to the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a while they stood there and then when they saw the others moving, then they moved. I could not see that. But for a while it stood stationary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was at that time you were not sitting down, you were part of the crowd at the back of the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other people had to force their way in behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you were looking into the interior of the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I pushed in I had to make room for the other two, so that the doors would close and so I turned around and I looked out. It was easier to look towards the door and I was on the step. It was easier than to look towards the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the "step", you mean the lower step where the doors operate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the first step, because there was three of us and maybe the three of us were on that last step.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those who had got on to the bus behind you between you and the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean between me and the door?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stepped on to the bus and you had to get your space and room. Then you told us you turned round and there were the people behind you who also had to get on after you. Were they between you and the folding doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I climbed and I made room for the other two. Then we were all standing on the same step and the door closed, and there was another step up and there were a lot of people on it and then the rest of them, I could not see how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see at that time. When we arrived in Keraterm I saw that a soldier was driving it in a uniform, but not on the bus, there was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it did not appear that there was a guard or guards within the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see. It was full. I could not even -- I could not even pass there. I was on the last step. It was impossible how full it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hedge that you had passed through to get on to the path to get on to the bus is a hedge that separates two of the houses, the house of Hamed Sivac and Munib Sivac, have I got that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of hedge is this? What height?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a couple of tree trunks and then there were smaller branches and it was not a fence. It was a natural, it was a growing fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was some shrub or something that had been used as a fence between the properties, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you walked through it, was there a hole there already or did you have to force your way through the branches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was already a hole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was part of the way through between those properties, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had to pass through that so that we could get to the path of Hamed Sivac to get on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hole that you got through was how far from the rear doors of the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five to seven metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to do that with your hands behind your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there already we were like this, bowed a little bit, and up until then we ran. After that we walked slower because of the crowd that was getting on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still with your hands behind your head, is that what you are indicating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nonstop, yes, nonstop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bowing of the head, presumably, made you look downwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the ground, or the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems from what you said that Dragoje Cavic was someone that you knew better than Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were getting on to the bus it was he that you were more concerned to see and look at as you knew each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Before I arrived I saw both of them. Afterwards, I looked at Cavic and Cavic sort of nodded his head as a greeting and lowered his rifle. I think he was a bit embarrassed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not until you were pushed by a weapon that you then turned, you say, to look at the other guard and you say that you then saw Dusko Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him beforehand, I just said that. As I was approaching, first I tried not to see, as it was people were moving slower I had to raise my hand and then I saw him and it was very clear. It was this far away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But until then you had not been conscious that it was Dusko Tadic. You had just seen a guard, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was aware that it was him because I know him from a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your head was bowed and you were looking downwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried. There we had to raise our heads because they all -- they all looked us in the eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you first asked to recollect what Dusko Tadic looked like and what he was wearing on this day on June 14th? When were you first asked to give that description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think now, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we are dealing with here are events that happened four years ago, are we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard any of these court proceedings on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only heard that he had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken to any other witnesses about descriptions of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your first recollection of what he actually looked like has been when you were asked now, you say, and do you think that you can be mistaken then about how that man looked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not mistaken, for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it seems, from what you have told us, that getting on the bus you did not look at him for a long period, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that. I said that I got on, that I turned towards the outside because it was easier to keep your head, your face, towards the glass rather than towards the people, and then I could see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned these two being guards at the door of the rear of the bus. Were there any other soldiers around there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There I did not see any. As we ran from the yard, they were directing us where we needed to go to and that is where I saw just the two. I think around Hamid Sivac's house there were also some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of them beating you as you went down the road from the collection point to where the bus was parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not then. Then it was only run on to the buses. They beat before that along the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, looking at the timing then, when your bus moved from this position, what time would that have been? How long had all this taken for you to be on that bus and then be taken on your journey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. I told you, altogether from my house it took about 10 minutes, waiting, running, provocation, standing in the yard waiting for those buses. It could have been -- we arrived in Keraterm around 4 o'clock, perhaps half past 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am interested in is what time you left Sivci.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you, and I am sure that it did not occur to anyone to look at their watch under the circumstances, nor did anybody dare to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but it may be with a little bit of thought and recollection that a time may suggest itself to you, even if you have not had time to think about it before. If you arrived at Keraterm at about 4 o'clock, did your journey there take about an hour from Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half past 3, 4 o'clock, I do not really know. I claim that I did not have a watch. I know that when I left my home it was warm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have told us it was about 1 o'clock that the soldier arrived at your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just one question, your Honour, I may ask for just a moment. Re-examined by MR. TIEGER Mr. Sivac, I may not have asked you this before, those panels which closed as a door on the back entrance of the bus, were those glass panels in part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had three or four sections, and they were as a harmonica and there were glasses on each side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have just a moment? Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour. Examined by the Court

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, how far is Sivci from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between Kozarac and Trnopolje, about three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, I do not know, looking at this map, this Prosecutor's 281, it would be two kilometres or so from Sivci to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know. We always said it was three. That is why I say, I went to school there, I went by car. Two and a half, three, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Trnopolje to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, from Sivci and Kozarac, Trnopolje is six kilometres, and this is about halfway closer to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three kilometres then from Sivci to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Sivac being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to calling the next witness there is a matter that we need to raise with the Court. The witnesses who will testify about the events in Jaskici have the same sensitivity that we faced with an earlier witness about naming particular persons whose bodies were found on that day, the same type of sensitivity. We do not wish to handle that matter through a closed session for each witness. So what we have proposed to the Defence (and they have agreed) is that we have listed people from the village on a list. We will have the witnesses refer to the list and give us the letters or numbers rather than mention names. Again, we are fully aware that the indictment is public, that any findings would be public. However, it is the sensitivities of the witness. So we believe this way we could accommodate them and at the same time get the information to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you then file that list under seal?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would submit that as a Prosecution Exhibit and ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- and have that provided to the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then that particular Exhibit would be under seal, I gather. Yes. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is not, your Honour, and it may be appropriate if you and your fellow Judges had a copy of the list as well with the key which is giving the numerical order and letters.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We will offer that now as a Prosecution Exhibit. It will be Prosecution Exhibit 285 for identification. We have provided a copy of this to the Defence and we have a copy for each of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 285?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would also ask at this time that we be allowed to put up a diagram that we will be using with the next several witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will you be offering a hard copy of that?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. We will be offering the large diagram as an Exhibit and a photograph can be made of that. We have a smaller diagram just showing the layout of the houses we will also be offering as an Exhibit. Your Honour, we would call Sena Jaskic. Sena Jaskic, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, would you please take the oath that is being given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MISS HOLLIS.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sena Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15th July '63.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Dergici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time if the witness could be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 280 which is a map. If I could ask you, ma'am,, to please look at that map for a moment to orient yourself and then I will ask you to show the Judges where the village of Dergici is located. If that could be put on the overhead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead, please. If you could move it over to the Kozarac area, please, and then zoom in on it. If you could please point to Dergici on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the map].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ma'am, did you live in Dergici until you married in 1981?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then move to your husband's home in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ismet Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is his nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, we could not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, ma'am, could you speak up just a bit. What was your husband's occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a wood cutter. That was his profession. He was a lumberer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your husband live with your husband's father in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your husband's father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huso Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lived in Jaskici until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Jaskici from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Jaskici from the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three, 3.5 kilometres I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time if I could have this marked as the next exhibit in order which should be Prosecution Exhibit 286 for identification. I have three copies for the Judges. We have already provided the Defence with a copy. Ma'am, would you look at that and, keeping in mind that the diagram is not exactly to scale, is this a correct layout of the houses in Jaskici as of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the map could be removed from the overhead projector and the diagram put on the overhead projector, please. As we look at this diagram, there appears to be a road or a path going to the homes of Abaz Jaskic and Nijaz Jaskic. To your knowledge, did that path continue all the way to Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to that behind the homes of Zijad Elkasovic, Ilijaz Elkasovic, Nijaz Elkasovic and Salko Jaskic, that area behind those homes, was that area fields?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were fields and this was a road to the fields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there also a small wood between Sivci and Jaskici, a small wooded area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take that pointer again and could you show us the approximate area where that small wooded area was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the map].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the small wooded area ran behind the house of Salko Jaskic and Nijaz Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the wooded area extend beyond that or did it stop with Nijaz Elkasovic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zijad Elkasovic's is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the small wooded area ran behind the fields up to the area of Zijad Elkasovic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you went to Sivci from Jaskici using the path by Abaz Jaskic's house or by going over the fields and through the wooded area, how long would it take you to walk from Jaskici to Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 286 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 286?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 286 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that the large diagram with the photographs be indicated as Prosecution Exhibit 287 for identification. At this time I would ask if the witness would, please, get up from the chair and come over to this diagram with the photos on it. If you could bring that pointer with you as well. If you can stand to the other side, please, nearer your chair. If I could ask you to point out certain things and, as I ask it, if you would point to it. First of all, for the Court would you please point to the photograph that shows the house of Zijad Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, that is the top left photograph as you look at the diagram. If you could next point to the photograph showing the house of Ilijaz Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the second photograph from the right, top right side as you look at the diagram, top left side as you look at the diagram. If you could please point to the house of Nijaz Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the third photograph from the top left as you look at the diagram. If you could point to the house of Salko Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the bottom photograph on the left side of the diagram as you look at it. If you could point to the homes of Abaz Jaskic and Nijaz Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Abaz Jaskic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you have indicated that the white two-storey structure is the home of Abaz Jaskic. If you can, could point to the home of Nijaz Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would note the witness is pointing to the red structure to the left of the photograph. If you could point to your home, the home of Huso Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the bottom right photograph as you view the diagram. If you could next point to the home of Ahmed Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the second photograph from the bottom on the right as you look at the diagram. If you could point to the photograph showing the home of Munib Jusovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the third photograph from the bottom on the right as you look at the diagram. If you could point to the home of Iso Nureski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the top photograph on the right as you look at the diagram. Finally, if you could point to the home of Jozo Orlovski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the photograph in the centre at the top of the diagram as you look at the diagram. Thank you. If you could please take your seat. I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 286 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: 287 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 287 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, you have pointed to the homes of the Elkasovic families. Did some people in Jaskici refer to the Elkasovic family as Elkaz as some type of nickname or abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some people did use it sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the Elkasovic families?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up or come closer to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, would you sit just a little bit further -- and perhaps the microphones can be turned now that she is sitting had in her chair -- so that we can hear you better.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, I know you are soft spoken but if you could assist us in speaking up a little it would help. Was Salko Jaskic any relation to Huso Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was Huso Jaskic's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ahmed Jaskic related to Huso?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ahmed was the brother of Huso Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his relationship then with Salko Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he related to Salko Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Huso Jaskic related to Salko Jaskic? What was the relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huso was Salko Jaskic's father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the Jaskic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You pointed to the photograph of the house of Munib Jusovic. What was his ethnic group, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Iso Nureski, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jozo Orlovski, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Catholic I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June of 1992 was the condition of the houses and other buildings, the yards, bushes and trees in Jaskici, on that date in June 1992 was the condition of the village the same as is shown in these photographs here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was much neater, tidier, cleaner and all the houses were in order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June of 1992 did men in uniforms come to Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when these men came to Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the summer kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph, please, marked as Prosecution Exhibit 288 for identification. If that can be shown to the Defence, please. Then if that could be provided to the witness. Is this a photograph of your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that photograph could be placed on the overhead projector, please. If you could zoom out a little bit more, please, to get the entire photograph. Thank you. Ma'am, as you look at this photograph, could you please point to the structure that was the house in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. This house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the structure in the centre of that photograph. Could you point ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please zoom back out, please. Could you please point to what you refer to as the "summer kitchen"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the smaller structure we see on the left of the photograph as we look at it, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The structure to the right of the photograph, what was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is was a barn and the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now as we look at this photograph and see the trees and the bushes, are those in the condition in which they were on 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not. Everything was clean and tidy and the house was all right and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the trees and bushes cut down lower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally, the trees were lower, everything had been felled, everything was fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on 14th June when the men came to the village of Jaskici you were in the small summer house, summer kitchen, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time who was in this summer kitchen with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband was there, Hasan Jakupovic, Nihada Turkanovic, Aisa, I do not know her surname, and my two daughters Jasmina and Merima.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were Hasan Jakupovic and Nihada Turkanovic, why were they at your home on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they had lost their homes already and had to be accommodated somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what villages did those people come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Aisa was from Brdjani and Hasan and Nihada were from Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nihada is Nihada Turkanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you first become aware that these men in uniform had come to your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were sitting there in the summer kitchen and there was gunfire daily, but then all of a sudden noise started and my husband stood up to see what was that, and then he said: "Here come some". He came back, sat down and there were already two soldiers at the door to the summer kitchen. It was all very quick.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this would be an appropriate time to break for lunch.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment). (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you continue with Mrs. Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Prior to that, your Honour, there is a matter I would like to clarify. During the testimony of Sakib Sivac, when he identified the accused, the transcript indicated that he said that the accused was wearing a white jacket.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then he corrected himself and said a "green jacket".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Actually, your Honour, that is what I thought as well when he said, "I am sorry, my mistake". In fact, the interpreter told me at lunch that the interpreter had misinterpreted, that in fact the witness said "green", the interpreter said "white". So the "I am sorry, my mistake" was, in fact, the interpreter speaking and not a translation from the witness. That was at 12.02.12, page 36, line 2. So I thought I would bring that to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We are fully aware of that, your Honour, so no problem whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Thank you. We will resolve that I accept that explanation, but we perhaps need to get some other matters clarified, just as a matter of policy. Fine. That has been clarified. Do you want to call Mrs. Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. MRS. JASKIC, recalled Examined by MISS HOLLIS, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Again, Mrs. Jaskic, I would ask you to try to speak up some so that the interpreters can hear your replies. When we broke for the lunch recess, you had indicated that on 14th June 1992, while you and other persons were in your summer kitchen, soldiers came to your door. Do you recall what time of the day it was that these soldiers came to your door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was 3 o'clock in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it that you know it was that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we were waiting for the news and just before the news it was the two soldiers came in. The news was supposed to be at 3 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was just at the time the news was to commence when the soldiers came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These two soldiers who came to your door, did you recognise either of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when these two soldiers came to your door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they came to the door they said that, "You two men come out and the rest of you remain seated".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they said, "You two men come out", who was it who left the summer kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband, Ismet, and Hasan Jakupovic and they took them towards the street, towards the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and the other people in the summer kitchen remain there in the summer kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see or hear after your husband and Hasan Jakupovic were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard when one of the soldiers cursed and I heard them beating my -- hitting my husband because he was breathing heavily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the soldiers ask any questions to the two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they cursed and I am quoting, "Alija, fuck your mother, who you have in the house?" and then they said, "Get up, get going" and such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear either of the two men reply and answer who was in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my husband said, "I do not have anybody".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then the noise, the shouts stopped and I could not hear anything any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later that day did you go out of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went out of the house that day what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the road and I went towards the Ilijaz's home and I saw two men dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the home of Zijad Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was between the two houses of Nijaz Elkasovic and Ilijas Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without giving the names of these two people, did you recognise these two people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could retrieve Prosecution Exhibit 285, please? If that Exhibit could be provided to the witness Mrs. Jaskic? Mrs. Jaskic, if you would look at that list, please, and if you could find the names of the two men whose bodies you recognised and, without giving the names, if you could tell the Judges the letters next to those names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letters A and B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you saw these two bodies, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned home. I took a bag with clothes and I took my children and went to Kararici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to Kararici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Kararici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your husband and Hasan were taken out that day, did you ever see either one of them again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was the last time I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look again at that list and if you could find the names of the men that you personally know were taken away that day and then without ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- giving the names if you could tell the Judges the numbers that are next to the names of those men who were taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. 6 and No. 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that Exhibit could be retrieved from the witness, please, and provided back to the Registry? Mrs. Jaskic, when you went to Kararici, did you stay in Kararici until 23rd June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that date did you go to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Trnopolje camp on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military came and all the refugees have to get their things and go to Trnopolje, so all the -- all of us refugees had to leave our houses and go to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, some soldiers. How do I know who they are?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day after arriving at Trnopolje camp, did you go on a convoy and eventually reach Bosnian government territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was your husband, Ismet, when he was taken away on 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question -- 31.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was 31 years old?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you have not seen him since that date. Have you made ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- attempts to find him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I looked all over, but in vain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you gone through international agencies to attempt to find him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any success at all in locating your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never had any success. I never found out anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was your husband a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary unit in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was he a member of any armed anti-Serb resistance group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband have any weapons in the home on the day he was taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No cross-examination, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Jaskic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for inviting me here. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Draguna Jaskic. DRAGUNA JASKIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, would you please take that oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not hear. I cannot hear very well. Jaskic Draguna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13th June 1955.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born in Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live there until you were 10 years old and then move to Kenjari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Kenjari a small hamlet that is near Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you move from Kenjari to Jaskici when you were married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jaskic Salko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was your husband born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: January 5th 1956.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your husband's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a worker. He worked in the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in Jaskici until 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could ask at this time that this be marked Prosecution Exhibit 289 for identification? Is this a photograph of your home in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If this could be placed on the overhead, please? Ma'am, if you could look at this photograph and if you could take that pointer that is on the table and if you could point to the building that was your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the building to the right in the photograph as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if you could tell us what the building is that is immediately adjacent, it is next to your house on the left, what was that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my summer kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if you could point to the building that is to the left of your summer kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could tell us what that structure was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the barn. It was of the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take your seat, please. As we look at that photograph, was that the condition that your home and the other buildings and your yard was in in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The trees and the bushes that we see there, were they shorter and cut back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they shorter and cut ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not like that. It was shorter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you grew up in Brdjani, in Kenjari and then as you lived in Jaskici, did you ever visit the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you visit Kozarac on an average in a week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two to three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would you visit Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would go to buy food, to buy supplies, to go to the marketplace, go with my parents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any relatives who lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was my mother and my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had they lived in Kozarac before the attack on Kozarac in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you regularly visit them in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him, I would see him in front of the cafe in the street, on the marketplace, in passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you would see him in front of the cafe. Do you know where his cafe was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were going on the main street of Kozarac and you were going in the direction of the Mutnik Mosque, what side of the street would Dule Tadic's cafe have been on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mutnik Mosque, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what businesses were across the street from Dule Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What businesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a hair salon, there was a pharmacy and a textile shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was Dule Tadic's cafe from your parents' home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 150 metres -- I am sorry, 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have indicated that you knew where Dule Tadic's cafe was. Did you ever go into that cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could give us an average, on average how often would you see Dule Tadic when you went to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended, sometimes twice, sometimes three times, sometimes not at all. It depends on the period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of Dule Tadic's family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Mira, his wife Mira.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what she did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was a nurse who worked in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His mother, Staka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you saw Dule Tadic as an adult, did you ever see him with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June 1992 were you at your home in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other people in the house with you on that day who did not live there with you and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Subha Mujic staying at your home at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is she related to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is she related?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She is my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were she and these other people staying at your house at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand, why, I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was your sister and these other people staying with you in your home at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see. They were there because their houses had been set on fire and they were expelled. They were refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What villages had these people come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Brdjani, Kamicani, Softici, Besici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic composition of these villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this day, 14th June 1992, were there men, women and children in your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that date did men wearing uniforms come to Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you first become aware that they were in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I heard the gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you heard the gunfire, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three soldiers came to my house and ordered us to come out, all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These three soldiers who came to your house, do you recall what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Black uniforms, black clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these three men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the three men ordered everyone to come out of the house. Did everyone in the house come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did come out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of the men in the house who came out of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were those men's names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, what were their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bejdo Balic, Sefik Balic, Salko Jaskic, Munib Besic and Sale Softic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Salko Jaskic was your husband. Were you related to Bejdo Balic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you related to Sefik Balic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you related to Munib Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my uncle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you related to Sale Softic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is my friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other four men, Sale Softic, Munib Besic, what were their ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came outside, the men, the women and the children, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, just a moment. A soldier entered the house, one of them, and he fired around the house and two were with us outside, men and us, women, and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened with the men, women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men were ordered to come out on to the road, and women and children were ordered to enter the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, men were first separated from the women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the men were first separated from the women and children, where were they told to go or where were they taken, to what position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With hands tied behind their neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could look at the picture of your house that is on the overhead projector and if we could see that? If you could take the pointer, please, and if you could show us where the women were told to stand when they were separated. So it was there at the bottom of your steps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the men were separated, where were the men taken or told to stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there at the edge of your barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you. When the men and the women and children were separated, and the men went to this spot near the edge of the barn, do you recall if there was any sand in that area where the men were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there was sand where they were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that at some point after that the men were ordered to go out on to the road and the women and children were ordered to go back into the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you began to go into the house, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Ismet Jaskic, my brother-in-law, and I saw Hasan, also a relative, I saw them walking by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw Ismet Jaskic and who else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hasan Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw them walking by, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them chased by Dule Tadic down the road towards my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say he was chasing them, he was running after them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was following them, going behind them, and he had a stick, a pole, in his hands and he was showing them to move ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him hit them with the stick in his hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see him hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ismet Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any injuries or wounds on Ismet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the right side. I could not see what there was. All I saw was blood. I could not see anything, but it seemed as if his whole part of the face -- of that part of the face had disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you saw Dule Tadic with Ismet and Hasan, in which direction were they going -- towards you or away from you on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were some 20 metres away from me when I saw them first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then as they approached you did they at some point stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they at some point stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they stopped, approximately how far away from you were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you saw them coming down the road toward you, what were you able to see of Dule Tadic? Were you able to see the front of him, the side of him? What were you able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw his face, from the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if he had any facial hair on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see after you saw Dule Tadic, Ismet and Hasan stop 10 metres away from you? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them come out to the road in front of my house, those five men that I have just listed, how Dule Tadic beats them with that stick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were still outside when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then go inside your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at your house again, the picture of your house, and if you could take the pointer and if you could show the Court where you were when you saw Dule Tadic with Ismet and Hasan and then with the other men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here in this part here in front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were on the steps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, at the end, at the bottom of the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph marked as Prosecution Exhibit 290 for identification? Mrs. Jaskic, you may sit down. If that could be shown to the Defence and then provided to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is that, 290?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Mrs. Jaskic, is that a photograph showing the road as it is taken from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the monitor, please? As we look at this photograph, can you tell us whose house it is that is across the road from yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] Ahmed Jaskic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we look at the trees and the shrubs in that photograph, on 14th June 1992 were they that high and unkempt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was all trimmed down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take that pointer and point to the place where you first saw Dule Tadic as he came down the road with Ismet and Hasan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you move the pointer in the direction they were moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us where they stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is near the edge of what appears to be a hedge on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could take your seat, please? Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibits 289 and 290.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 289 and 290 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, when you went into the house what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was ordered to lie down, that we all enter the house and lie down on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went down on to the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you get up and look out the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got up and looked out the window what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Dule Tadic beat my family, my father, brother, husband, brother-in-law, uncle, friend -- my whole family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While Dule Tadic was there beating these men, were there other soldiers there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then after you saw Dule Tadic beating your relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Other soldiers were bringing water and pouring water over them when they would faint. They were .....

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw my brother move nearer to my father, to try to come nearer to my father and he grabbed him by his trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw these men out there being beaten, where were they lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road in front of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what position were they lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With face down on the sand and hands behind the neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of these men resisting as they were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see then after you saw your brother, Sefik, grab on to your father's legs, what did you see next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw my father trying to stand up, and I saw Dule strike him again with a stick behind the neck and he fell again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I fell again. My son would not let me go on looking, and he kept me on the floor saying, "Don't look, they are alive" and I said that "None of them were alive". Then he pulled me back to the floor and said, "Mum, they are still alive". So I waited and when I stood up he had made them all move towards Kozarac down the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you stood up you looked out the window again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked out the window what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that he was beating Jasmin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the men still lying on the road or were the men now gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up they were standing, those men were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what did you see after you saw him beating Jasmin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them, they had gone down the road, that is, he stayed there beating Jasmin and then Jasmin followed and they all went down the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "he was beating Jasmin", who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "they went down the road". In what direction did they go back, towards Huso's house or up the road in the direction of Zijad's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Zijad's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you stood in your house looking out the window how far from the window were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were 10 metres away from your window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were two metres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the wall, two metres away from the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was Dule Tadic from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
