utterances.text: 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you looked through the window, did you have a clear view of what was happening outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you looked through the window from inside the house, what did you see of Dule Tadic? Did you see the front of him, the side of him, the back of him? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The front. I looked him in the face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you think about this entire incident, both when you were outside and saw Dule Tadic and when you were inside and saw Dule Tadic, in total how long do you think you looked at Dule Tadic during this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 minutes, about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have document 9.15 marked as Prosecution Exhibit 291 for identification? If you could show that to the Defence, please? Mr. Jaskic, could you look at that photograph? Is that photograph a view as seen out of the window that you were looking through that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The window, yes, but it did not look like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there glass in the window on 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put that on the overhead, please? If you could again take the pointer and for the Court if you could point to where you saw Dule Tadic as you looked from the window and saw him beat the men on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can be seated, please. I tender Prosecution Exhibit 291 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 291 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were watching this occurring outside the window, was your sister Subha watching as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall saying anything to your sister as you were watching Dule Tadic beating your relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we said, "Look at our family down there".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would please look around the courtroom and see if Dule Tadic from Kozarac is in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is over there sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is him. He has a green jacket and a shirt, a tie. That is the man.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note the proper identification of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sometime after the men were taken away, did you go outside your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything on the road where the men had been lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you went outside, did you see any bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without mentioning the name of anyone, did you recognise any of these bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close did you come to these men's bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two metres and less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to recognise these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Their clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If Prosecution Exhibit 285 could be provided to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, do you have 285? (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, I am going to ask you to look at that list and if you could keep that in front of you, please? If you could look at the list first and, without giving anyone's names, if you could see the men, the five men, whose bodies you recognised and then if you could tell the Court the letter that is next to the names of those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter A, letter B, letter C, letter D, letter E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at that list again and, again without mentioning the names, if you could tell the Court the numbers which are beside the names of the men you know were taken away from Jaskici on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No. 1, No. 2, No. 3, No. 4, No. 5, No. 6, No. 7, No. 8, No. 9, No. 10, No. 11, No. 12, No. 13, and No. 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that could please be retrieved and returned to the Registry, thank you. Did you ever see Sale Softic again after 14th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second day, two days, two days after ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two days after the incident in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had gone out and seen those bodies, realised what men had been taken from the village, did you become aware of any men who were left in the village? Were there any men at all left in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of the men who were left in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huso Jaskic remained, Zijad Elkasovic and Munib Jusovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the age of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were men of 60, 66, 68, somewhere like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Jaskici later that day and go to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that same day we left Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then go on a convoy and eventually reach Bosnian government territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this day in Jaskici on 14th June, have you ever heard from or been in contact with your husband, your father or your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never to date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you made any attempts to locate them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have those attempts been successful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were all in vain, all attempts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, do you recall being visited by members of this Tribunal in May 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a member of this Tribunal showing you a book of photographs on that date, asking you to look at those photographs and asking if you recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were asked if you recognised anyone in that photo book, what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remained silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you indicated you did not recognise anyone, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If, in fact, you recognised Dule Tadic, why did you say you did not recognise him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know. I had a reaction from fear. I do not know myself. I kind of lost it. I became afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you later asked by Tribunal personnel about a reaction you had had to one of the photographs you had been shown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Tribunal personnel at that time that you did not identify Dule Tadic because you were not sure it was him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told this court today that it was Dule Tadic in your village. Why did you tell Tribunal personnel that you were not sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply I was afraid. I had a reaction and then I did not say it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Realising the importance of being absolutely honest with these Judges in this Tribunal, I will ask you again if on 14th June 1992 did you recognise ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- Dule Tadic as the man in your village beating a man in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did I tender Prosecution Exhibit 288, your Honour? We are not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would tender it. That was the photograph of Samir Jaskic's house. In addition to that, your Honour, I am not sure we tendered the video of Sivci. That was Prosecution 283. At this time I would tender that as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. 283, I know, was not tendered, well, my records show it was not tendered. What do you show, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 288?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 288 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While I am still standing, could I ensure that I tendered 289?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is admitted 289. Regarding 283, that was the video that Mr. Tieger used this morning?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. That was a video clip of Sivci.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 283?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. 283 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay? Cross-Examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right, Mrs. Jaskic, is it not, you were shown some photographs in a book, was it a year ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you receiving any ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if Mr. Bos can check the channel?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think she is getting it. Why do you not repeat the question? Why do you not repeat the question, Mr. Kay, and just try again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I will. That is right. You were shown a book of photographs, was it a year ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the date, but they were showing me photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was? How long ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how much time passed. I do not know what date it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked at those photographs, you did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- identify anyone that you had been ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- asked ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dusan. Yes, Dusan Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, wait until Mr. Kay finishes the question and then when he has finished, then you answer. Excuse me, Mr. Kay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. [To the witness]: Did there come another occasion when you were questioned about those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know a single date. I only know 14th June because I remember that exactly. The rest I do not know and I still do not remember it to date. Since the war I do not, I have not, I only remember that date when my husband, my father, my family had been taken away. That remained in my memory, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can see if you can help me as to when it was you were asked again about the photographs, how long ago from today's date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a poor memory, Mrs. Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked at those photographs, you did not see anyone you recognised, that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no, I recognised Dusan Tadic but I did not react. I was afraid. I was -- I got excited. I had a reaction. I stand behind that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told someone at the time that you did not recognise Dusko Tadic in those photographs, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not tell an investigator for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not tell an investigator for the Prosecution that you did not recognise Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object to this. This is misleading in that she was never asked if she recognised Dusko Tadic. She was asked if she recognised anyone in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It might be better if we hear the evidence from the witness rather than what the Prosecution believes to have been said.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, but on direct examination the question was: "Were you asked if you recognised anyone in the photographs?" and her answer was: "Yes, I was asked that". That is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Prosecution have asked a leading question and sought a reaction from the witness in relation to that question. The Defence are entitled to find out from this witness what was actually said. It seems here that the procedure that has been followed by the Prosecution has provided them with a non-identification and there has been an attempt to try to put this in a positive way, your Honour, which is a proper basis for the Defence to explore what evidence is sought to be brought before the Court by this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The question, I think, the concern that one of the Judges may have is whether or not this witness would have known that it was an investigator -- is that your concern?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: If you want to find out what was said to her, you should ask her. You are putting things.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Was that your objection, it was misleading?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were you asked when you were shown the book of photographs, Mrs. Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked me if I recognised anybody on that photograph and I was surprised when I saw Dusan Tadic, and I got excited and even got scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who asked you that question was who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. -- I forget the name. I do not remember the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what his job was? Did you know why he was showing you those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He showed me the photograph and said if, could I recognise anybody. He did not say whom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of it you said you did not recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not, but then they visited me again and they said why did I not say, and I told them that I got scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who visited you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a reaction, Mr. -- I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paepen? Mr. Paepen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paepen, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who visited you again to say, why you did not say? What did they mean by that? Do not look over there, please, Mrs. Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, she can look. I do not think the Prosecutor is coaching any answers, but obviously the witness is nervous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will watch Miss Hollis. Miss Hollis was not going to give her any answers. That is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I mean, there is no way for her to give her an answer with a nod or whatever, but go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When they visited you again and said, "Why did you not say?" what did they mean about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I recognised, why did I not say, and I said that I had a reaction, that I was surprised, that I was scared and that is why I did not say it. If I recognised, I said who it was, why did I not say that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said -- they said if I recognised who it was in that picture and I said, "Dusan Tadic".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they came to you the second time, did they have the photographs with them again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not look at another book of photographs after that first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you which photograph you had not recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked at these photographs, had you seen any news about the arrest of Dusko Tadic in the newspapers or on the television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- God forbid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that, that you had not seen any programmes about the arrest of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am sure I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you watched any programmes that have dealt with events ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that once. That is enough for me. I want peace. I have had enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But have you seen any on the news on television whilst other events ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- and other events have been ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw that live. I did not see anything after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you watch any television or news programmes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you watch television at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes a film or something with the children. I do not have much time. I am not interested at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been asked to look at photographs of Jaskici and the gardens in front of the houses. Of course, when this happened it was a different time of year, was it not? It was in the summer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was four years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This road through Jaskici is a road that has hedges alongside it, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer time there are a lot of leaves on the trees and leaves on those hedges, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but that hedge was this and because I was standing it, I know. It was, you know, a very low one, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you looked out of that window from your house, can you see the road when you look out? It is not asphalt, is it? It is an unmade road? Can you actually see the lane, the surface of the lane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the road. It is not a real road. It is a Macadam road. I could see it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the right-hand side there is a hedge as you look out of your window, and that is quite a thick hedge, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at that time it was not that dense. Now it is, but at that time it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that hedge was to protect the land from the fields? There was a field the other side of the hedge, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was a house -- that was my husband's uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the area behind that hedge was grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which side are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you look out of your window and on the right-hand side as you look at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was the road, at one time it was a real road, but now it has all been grown in because everybody has been expelled. That was a real road, but now it is all grown in to grass and bushes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were originally outside and your men who had been in the house were separated from you, can you remember how many soldiers were generally in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw two, one was going with Dule Tadic, there were three in front of my house, so there were five. I do not know about other parts, but this is where I was. I saw them, five soldiers, five Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the men who had been in your house and were beside the barn, can you recollect when they moved from the front of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While they were searching the house and looking for arms and shooting, and then they just left and they said, "Let's go", that they should come with them and we should go back into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went back into the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time were the men being moved away from the area where they were originally standing by the barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were leading the men out, because there were a lot of us outside before we got back into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the soldiers who had come to your house then moved those men on to the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they just standing there for a period of time or what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were bringing water to pour over men who were on the ground who were beaten up, so that they could get up so that Dule Tadic could drive them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other soldiers who were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the others? You may not have known their names but did you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- recognise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw Dule Tadic and I recognised him and the others I did not recognise. I looked at him the most because he was there because he was beating, so that is why I saw him the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that the soldiers who came to your house had black uniforms, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were black t-shirts, black pants, black bandannas and gloves with no fingertips.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The trousers that they wore, can you remember if they were black as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any markings on these black clothes to indicate anything about the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not see anything. That is ----

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I could not catch that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you repeat that please, Mrs. Jaskic? The interpreters did not hear you. Repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Black clothes, black t-shirts, black pants, black bandanna, a ribbon and black gloves with the finger tips cut off, no fingers that was -- they were bare.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they have any weapons with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what kind they were? Were you able to identify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with weapons. I only know that they were rifles. I am not a soldier. I was not in the army, but it is the weapons that kill, some kind of rifles. I do not know which ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dule Tadic, you said, was running down the road with a long stick or pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not run. He walked slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone running down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were going in front of him and he beat them and my -- he was being beaten and he was staggering from one side of the road to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he was beating them with? What was that implement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a stake, a wooden stake, like a stick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- I did not measure it but it was about 1.5 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapons did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A rifle, what kind, I do not know, but he had -- he had it slung around on his shoulder and he carried that stake in his hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any beret or hat on his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see it. At that time he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about his facial hair.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was grown in, I do not know how much, so there was a beard. I cannot say exactly but he was, sort of, grown in, unkempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were indicating with your fingers by your face then. Are you able to say whether it was a full beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was -- it was grown in. I did not have time to look at it. I only know it is a beard. I wish I had time to look at it more closely, but I know he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not have very long to observe him then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did have enough time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked that because you said you wished you had longer to see about the beard. Is ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- it the case here that you are describing something that did not take very long at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 minutes I was looking at him, at that spot, Dule Tadic. I know Dule Tadic well. That is your opinion. I know what I saw and what I think. I stand by my statement, by my opinion, and what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (4.20 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. [To the witness]: Can you remember, Mrs. Jaskic, what time this was on 14th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 3.00 or half past 3, I do not know exactly, but ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you saw Dusko Tadic coming up the lane with the stick, were there any other soldiers with him or was he just on his own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was another soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the lane outside your house, can you remember how many soldiers were there? Can you tell me the number, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with Dusan there was the soldier that came with him and another three. Five soldiers there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the total number of soldiers you saw in the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Outside in the lane how many people from the Jaskici village you described as your family, what was the number of people that were there and on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your men folk who had been taken and kept in the lane there for that period of about 10 minutes, you say, can you remember how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken about this case with your sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as your sister's name is, can you give that to us, what her name is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may confer as long as you wish. We need some time. Mr. Kay, would you mind repeating your last two questions? As I recall, the questions were, how many soldiers were there in the lane when Mrs. Jaskic saw them. Then the second question was: "How many of your family were out there at that same time?" Would you mind repeating those two questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I have to repeat these questions to you again, Mrs. Jaskic, for technical reasons. Can you remember how many soldiers were in the lane with the men during the 10 minutes that you were observing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five soldiers, Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Dusko Tadic came up the lane with the stick, was he on his own or with any other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a soldier, Serb soldier, with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how that soldier was dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how many men folk from your village of Jaskici were out there in the lane, what the number was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eight. They were lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no redirect. Examined by the Court

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, I just have one question. When you first came in today and you were taking the oath, it appeared to me that you were having some difficulty reading the words that are on the oath. May I ask you, what is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Miss Hollis, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Jaskic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jaskic, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will next call Mr. Jos Paepen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have something to say at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is a matter that arises from the examination and cross-examination of the previous witness, that is, we have some hesitation when discussion between the parties and the Bench is also translated, because we feel that the witness might anticipate to what has been discussed when the question is repeated after a ruling from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We would rather prefer the witness not to understand what is being discussed between either party, that is, counsel and the Bench, the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What question are you referring to specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: For example, the question about shown the photograph, was that a photograph of Dusko Tadic? Then an objection arose. I would say that we have not to exclude the possibility that the witness listening to what the discussion is about may anticipate in the next answer.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am trying to recall what was the discussion. There was a concern, I know ----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was exactly the question.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- that one of the Judges had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. So, by the Prosecution it was stated that the right question that was put to the witness was, quote answer, and then the witness hearing all this used exactly the same phrase. So we want to exclude that possibility by not having it translated if any discussion on tactical matters will arise.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me just a minute. May I confer with my fellow Judges? Thank you. (The learned Judges conferred) Mr. Wladimiroff, if you will, you can refer us -- of course, we do not have the transcript -- if you want to, you can handle it tomorrow. We can look at the transcript, we might be able to better follow you and be able to address your concern more fully. In some systems, of course, we approach the Bench to resolve all of these matters as we have talked about among ourselves, and many thought that that is something we should try to avoid as much as possible. Let me just take a look at the transcript and, if you will, you can point us to your concern and then I will be able to answer it directly tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. MR. JOS PAEPEN, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I solemnly declare I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated thank you. Examined by MISS HOLLIS.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Paepen Josef.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you work in the Office of the Prosecutor for the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you worked for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I work in the Office of the Prosecutor since 1st July 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1995 were you working as an investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 31st May 1995 did you go to the residence of Draguna Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that date did you show her a photo book containing 13 photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that date did you ask her to withhold comment until she had reviewed all 13 photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then tell her that if she recognised anyone in the photographs, she should say that or she should also say if she did not recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I showed the book to her, I told her, I asked her to withhold every comment until the moment that she had seen all the photos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When she had seen all the photos, what was she to tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After she saw all the photos of the book, she said that she did not know anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you turn the pages of the book for her showing her the photographs one by one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she review all 13 photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you indicated, she told you that she did not recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was showing the pictures, she did not say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end when you asked her if she recognised anyone, what did she say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That she did not know anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were showing her the photographs, did Draguna Jaskic have an unusual reaction to any of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She had -- when I showed her the pictures, the first two, she was nodding her head, and then the third picture, when I showed that picture, she had an immediate reaction. She was tense. Her eyes were growing bigger. She was moving on her chair, and she was like "huh", so expelling forcibly her breath. This was at the third picture. Then the other pictures, there was no reaction until the ninth picture where she was like hesitating, but then she said, "Go on". No reaction any further for the last pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there only one photograph to which she had such a strong reaction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the third picture that I showed her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a photograph of whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the photograph of Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination? Cross-Examined by MR. KAY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paepen, how long did it take to go through the photo book with her from the first picture to the end picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was showing the book to her, I had the book in front of me, on this level, and I was turning the pages one by one, giving her all the time that she needed to see the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she indicate to you when she wanted the pictures to be turned on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I told, sir, for the first picture she nodded her head. When she nodded her head, at that moment I went further to the second picture. At that time there was the same reaction. She nodded again her head. Then the third picture, since that reaction was the immediate reaction and tensing, she said, "Dalje, go on". At that moment I went on to the following picture, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After picture No. 9, she also told you to go on as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the picture No. 9 she said also "Go on", but there was only like a slight hesitation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Go ahead, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I stopped there as I could see your Honours conferring. [To the witness]: After you had been through the album, did she ask to look at any photographs again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When she went through the pictures, all the pictures, at that moment she said, I asked her the question if she said, had recognised somebody in that album. She said, "No".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did not ask to see any of the photographs ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this take, this process between you and her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole process of going through the pictures, I would say this would be -- the exact time, I cannot tell you, sir, but it would be around five minutes that she had this to go through the 13 pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you with her on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this occasion, I do not recall the exact time, sir, of that. I cannot tell you that exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any notes at the time as to what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that she went through the pictures, I took a note of the whole procedure, what had been, how it had been done and about the reactions that she had had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Does that tell you how long it was, the process, how long you were with her for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not put that in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not, for instance, put down when you arrived and when you left her company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have nothing further -- excuse me, your Honour, I am terribly sorry. Your Honour, there are no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour. Examined by the Court

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Paepen, did you then go back to speak with Mrs. Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never went back to Mrs. Jaskic. I was only in contact with her for this photospread, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the number of photos in the photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sure you could not answer this question, but may be so. Let me put it this way: We have received a number of copies -- three, I guess -- of the photo book. As I recall, the photos were arranged differently in the different photo books. By any chance, do you have with you a copy of the photo box that was actually given to Mrs. Jaskic when you met with her in May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not, your Honour. I handed the book over again after my mission to the team who was investigating the case.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Miss Hollis, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No additional questions, your Honour, but we have reproduced a copy of that book, if the Court wants it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it should come in to make his testimony complete because there is reference to photo books. As I have indicated, there are photo books and photo books. I even asked that when they are submitted they be submitted in a way so that the photo is permanently affixed so that the photo does not come out and, perhaps, the Registry may run into a problem. So, it seems to me that we should have the photo book if we are talking about it, let us have it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you want the photo book itself or a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The copy of the photo book that this witness showed Mrs. Jaskic. That is what I think is important.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I have this here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Why do you not show that to the Defence -- or how should we handle this? All I want is a copy, but I want to make sure that the Defence has an opportunity to see what will be coming into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I agree with your Honour's procedure for this, and so that we all know which particular witness has what sequence of photographs. If a photo copy of that book was provided for the Defence, we would be happy with that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Then you will offer that without objection as Exhibit No. ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It will be 292, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. 292 will be admitted as a copy of the photo book that was shown to Mrs. Jaskic on May 31st 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do have a matter arising from your Honour's questioning. Further cross-examined by MR. KAY Mr. Paepen, the photo book that you had shown this witness, Mrs. Jaskic, had you shown that same photo book to other potential witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the first time you had been involved in a photo identification through the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With this book, yes, sir, but in this case it was the first time I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the only occasion that you have been involved with a photo identification in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis? Re-examined by MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paepen, do you know if this photo book was used again after it being shown to Mrs. Jaskic since she did not identify anyone in the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know because I was only for this occasion involved in this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Is there any objection to Mr. Paepen being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you wish this book now? May we make a copy of it first?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you can go ahead and make a copy of it. My only concern is that the Defence is satisfied that what comes in as 292 is the actual photo. I am sure the two of you can work that out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go on to another witness a matter of law does arise here. It may be appropriate if we raise that matter now. That concerns the status of this particular evidence with the non-identification at the time by the witness saying that she did not recognise anyone within the particular photo book and the use of the evidence at a later stage by the Prosecution with an explanation or comment by the witness as to her feelings at the time and, indeed, saying that she did recognise. Your Honour heard her evidence earlier this afternoon. Our submission on this matter is that there should be no positive adduction of this evidence before the Court because of the fact that it remains as an unreliable and unsafe identification in all these circumstances. We are concerned about this evidence having been adduced in this form. Within most jurisdictions, it would not have been used.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want a ruling? Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think it would be appropriate for it to be a ruling because it is something that ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Not at this point. Actually, I was surprised that you did not object to the testimony of Mr. Paepen. I do not know, I mean, he was giving his view of when she nodded, but it comes in and it goes to the weight. With respect to this whole issue, it is my understanding that you will be calling an expert witness to explain, from your point of view, how these photospreads should be handled. This is one witness, I am sure, that your expert will speak to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That may well be the case, but it is a matter of law as to whether the evidence is admissible in the first place, when the procedure itself has produced the evidence that the witness said she did not recognise the defendant. We considered whether we should make an objection in advance, but we felt that we would have to tell the Bench what the evidence was going to be and there would have been no point in giving it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. What you are submitting, I suppose, is a motion to exclude her testimony regarding the photospread book and the testimony of Mr. Paepen as well or just hers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The two are related.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Both of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. We will take that under advisement and advise you tomorrow how we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to respond? I am sorry, I just went right over you. Go ahead. What is your position regarding this?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: First of all, your Honour, I would suggest that, given these circumstances, we do not have a non-identification. Had the witness responded as she did when shown the photo book, "I do not recognise anyone", and thereafter had continued to say, "I do not recognise anyone", then in my jurisdiction (and I think most jurisdictions) certainly Mr. Paepen would not be able to come on and testify as to her reaction to the photo, to show some type of identification through her reaction. However, this witness has said that, indeed, she did recognise the individual in No. 3. That was consistent with a very observable reaction she had to that photograph. She has come to this court and provided an explanation. Certainly all of those circumstances must be considered in determining what weight you will give to her testimony, but the Prosecution would suggest that there is not a basis in law for striking the testimony itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask you something? This was a case of what you would call a recognition witness, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Why was she shown the photo book at all?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Early on in what we were doing with many of these witnesses, your Honour, with the Office of the Prosecutor was still engaged in investigative work as well as identification, as the Defence has pointed out, is in an issue in many of these cases. With all the uncertainties we have in a case such as this, then often recognition witnesses were shown books. I believe we have had other recognition witnesses who were shown books as well. We had not developed a full policy and it was still in part an investigative effort.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are entitled to rely on this evidence from the fact that there was no recognition of the defendant by the witness when she considered the photo book. That would have been something we could have adduced through the officer in the case or even through Mr. Paepen. As I understand Mr. Paepen's evidence, it was not that the witness recognised anyone. In fact, it was the contrary. The witness said she did not know anyone within the book. So our submission is that the Prosecution have attempted through the witness to say she did recognise someone, when the evidence at the time was that she did not. That is really our complaint about this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will take a look at the transcript. The reason that I asked Mr. Paepen about the second visit and whether or not he was the person who visited the witness the second time was, as I understood the testimony, that is when she then explained her position and, I gather, did make a recognition through the book although she did not have the book then. What she said is -- Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I had asked a specific question whether there was a book.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exactly, she did not have the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand that. The motion that you have filed regarding the use of the book, as I understand the motion -- it was several weeks ago -- would exclude the use of the photo book if the witness knew Mr. Tadic before ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- under all circumstances. That is a motion that you have indicated that you will hold in abeyance pending the offering of expert witness ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- expert witness on your behalf. So that is, of course, one of the issues that we have to keep in mind. That is what Judge Stephen was talking about, why was the Prosecution even showing them when she has visited Kozarac perhaps three times a week and her parents live 100 and whatever it is metres away from Mr. Tadic's cafe? I think we have the positions of the parties. You want us to exclude this evidence regarding the use of the photo book. That is something that we can talk about and tell you tomorrow after we look at the transcript, if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Do you really want to exclude the evidence? I thought you wanted to use the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. I was taking it two ways. What I was seeking to exclude was the Prosecution attempt to have a positive identification from their material with a witness giving an inconsistent account on a later occasion. As we are discussing this matter, your Honour, it may be that it would assist your brother Judges and all parties if we did deal with this during Professor Wagenaar's testimony. It might be more appropriate at that stage.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am certain that you will and you will because one of the major points in your earlier motion that you filed several weeks ago was that that is tainted, the use of the photo book is tainted, if the witness knows Mr. Tadic already. So that is the first thing that I am considering as I heard this witness is, what are the parameters that we should decide on, and even thinking about whether we will listen to this witness's identification. But back to Judge Stephen's point, do you want us to exclude the evidence or do you want us to rule that there was a non-identification in the photospread?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the point, your Honour, that there was a non-identification in the photospread.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We would have been entitled to this material under the disclosure rules because it was evidence that went to a matter of concern to the Defence, an inconsistent matter. In those circumstances, the Prosecution would have had to have disclosed it to us and we would have decided how we would have used this particular material. It has come up this way as it is the Prosecution who have been adducing the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So do you want the Chamber then to rule as to whether or not there was a non-identification by this witness through the use of the photospread? Is that what you want us to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: A few minutes ago you said, perhaps, it should be delayed until Dr. Wagenaar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was being helpful, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You just tell me what you want and we will consider it, that is for sure, this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It occurred to me as we were discussing it that it might be appropriate to deal with all these matters in the one hearing relating to Professor Wagenaar. I will look to my leader for his confirmation on that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So then we do not have to stay late tonight and consider this? Very good. OK. Miss Hollis, do you understand that? We will just move right along. Would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We would call Subha Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just while this witness is being brought in, there are two matters that you put to me yesterday for reply, one relating to when we anticipate completing the evidence. We anticipate that to be 16th August, Friday 16th August. Your Honours also asked how long after speaking with the Defence witnesses we would need to complete our enquiries concerning our rebuttal of alibi evidence. We would seek three weeks, if that is acceptable to the court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection from the Defence regarding the three weeks to submit rebuttal evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then you will have three weeks to submit the rebuttal list of witnesses, as I recall, under the Rules after you complete speaking with the Defence alibi witnesses. We will enter an order to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: August 16th, of course, as has been the case with your listing of witnesses, that does not include any estimate of cross-examination, obviously, because that is not something that you can handle?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Miss Hollis, call ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Subha Mujcic, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- Subha Mujic. MRS. SUBHA MUJIC was called

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Registry has advised me that this witness would need to have the oath read to her.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you state your full name, ma'am? What is your name? Can you hear me? THE WITNESS [In translation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you repeat your name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subha Mujic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat after me? "I"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Repeat your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mujic Subha.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "Solemnly declare".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "That I will speak the truth".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "The whole truth".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "And nothing but the truth".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You understand you are taking this or making this declaration this oath and that by doing so you are attesting that you will tell the truth today, is that your understanding, Mrs. Mujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, would you tell us your date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 7th December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born in Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Brdjani near the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Brdjani from the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in Brdjani until 26th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 26th May 1992 did you go to Trnopolje detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After several days at Trnopolje detention camp were you allowed to go to the home of your sister in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your sister's name who lives in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Draguna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is her last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, what is your ethnic group or nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, during the time you were growing up and then living in Brdjani as an adult did you ever go to the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you go to the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went when there was a market and I went to my mother's on Saturdays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your mother lived in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war about four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew him. My son told me that he was karate trainer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of any businesses that he had in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He worked that karate and he had a cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that cafe was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac. When you go down Marsala Tita Street, down towards the road, Banja Luka/Prijedor Road, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you are going down the main street toward the Banja Luka/Prijedor Road Dule Tadic's cafe is on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, down Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Toward the Banja Luka/Prijedor Road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His cafe is on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what businesses are across from that cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a hair salon, a barber's salon and a medicine, I cannot, oh, yes, the pharmacy and a textile shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would go to Kozarac to visit your mother and to do your shopping, on average how often would you see Dule Tadic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would sometimes see him weekly, sometimes every other week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him to see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever socialise with Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew the mother and the wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the wife's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the mother's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Staka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you last saw Dule Tadic before the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe a month before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the four years that you knew Dule Tadic to see him, did you ever see him with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This month or so before the attack on Kozarac when you saw Dule Tadic, do you recall whether or not he had facial hair at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall, did he have facial hair or did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June 1992 where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit Jaskici often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, once a month, once every two months, depending on the free time that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June when you were in Jaskici at whose house were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Salko Jaskic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you there at your sister's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was there in my sister's house, because I did not have another place. I could not be at my home in Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had happened to your home in Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was shelled and the house was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This area of Brdjani where you lived, what was the nationality of the inhabitants there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 289, please. Mrs. Mujic, do you recognise what is shown on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my sister's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the house of Salko Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and of Salko Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 14th June 1992 were there men, women and children in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that date did men wearing uniforms come to Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you first become aware that they had come to Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they drove us out we saw that it was the military, the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say they drove you out, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they took us out. They lined up the men and us they put alongside the house, and one soldier came into the house and shot around the house, and they said that they would shoot anybody who would go and see. The men were driven down the road and we were returned back into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If could I stop you there for a moment. You said that you were taken outside the house and the men were separated from the women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the men were separated from the women and children where were the women told to stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, next to the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the men told to stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men were lined up near the garage at a heap of sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could have that photograph put on the overhead projector. Mrs. Mujic, if you could take the pointer that is there and if you could point to where the women and children were told to stay. If you could point on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here is where women and children were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could also point to where the men were taken to stand near the pile of sand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, this is where men were next to that sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
