utterances.text: Can you point to the building that you called the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. The garage is where the car went into the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is to the far left on the photograph as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were outside and the men and the women were separated, you were then ordered to go back into the house, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you went into the house could you see what was being done with the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw they beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw this while you were still outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone who was beating the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the men who were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic I recognised, he beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whom did he beat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Bejdo Balic that Dule Tadic beat, Salko Jaskic, Bejdo Balic, Munib Softic and Ismet Jaskic and Hasan Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now had you known ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Jasmin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Jasmin's last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his mother's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zemka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now after you saw Dule Tadic beating these men did you then go into the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were outside and you saw Dule Tadic doing this, did you have a clear view of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw clearly and surely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what Dule Tadic was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether at that time he had facial hair or he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what he was beating the men with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not -- I do not understand that, whether he had a rifle or something like this, I do not know, a rifle, and then he beat with that and with his boots, with his feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back into the house what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they told us not to look, but I had to look because it was our family. So I looked and I thought let them kill me too. Then I watched as he beat them until they fell unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see beating the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were inside watching this, you were watching through a window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can tell us, do you know how far you were away from that window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were from the window maybe about this much, this distance. I do not know if it is one metre, a metre and a half, two metres. I was so scared I was not thinking about that and I did not think that I would survive at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were close to the window when you were watching this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see clearly through the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could see clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked through the window and saw these beatings that were occurring, where were the men that had been taken out of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were led outside and they had to hold their hands like this, and then they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they were being beaten where were they at that point? Were they still in the yard or had they been moved somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, outside. They had them lie down and they had to have their hands over their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it that they made them lie down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the road behind the fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see after you saw Dule Tadic beating the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then what I saw is they jumped over the fence and he ordered to pour water on them so they would get up, and then the soldiers went over to Ahmed's house and then they brought water to pour over them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say they jumped over the fence. What fence are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a fence on the yard at my sister's house and then there was a road. They were on the side of the road. They did not open anything. They just jumped over. So that one just crossed or jumped over and poured the water over them, so that they would come to, the water that we used for laundry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said you saw them go to Ahmed's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was Ahmed. What was his last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Prosecution Exhibit 291, please. If the previous Exhibit could be retrieved for the Registrar. Mrs. Mujic, do you recognise the view through that window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it. This is the window of my sister's from which we were looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please. Could you take the pointer again, Mrs. Mujic, and could you point to where Dule Tadic was beating the men as you looked out the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph]. We were watching from here and this is where he was. There is the road, there behind. This is Ahmed's house towards Huso Jaskic and on that road there was a fence there, and this is where they jumped over this soldier and this is where Dule beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there was a fence there. What side of the road was the fence on? Was it on Ahmed's side or on Salko's side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Salko's side there was an iron fence and on Ahmed's side it was a wooden fence. So they jumped over Salko's fence and came to the well and there was a trough behind this well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This iron fence, were you able to see over or through that fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That fence was a low one, not high, because we were looking and it was an iron fence like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to look over that fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see the men led away on that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take the pointer and if you could show us the direction in which they were led.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] Up this road towards those houses up there and towards Kozarac. That is where the road leads. This is the road, then Huso Jaskic's house next to it and then the houses that come next. It is all up towards Kozarac. As they were taken, then we have not seen or heard from them since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please at this time look around the courtroom and tell you us if you see Dule Tadic from Kozarac in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where he is sitting and what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can tell you, between these two policemen, a green jacket and a cream collar shirt and a tie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the man that you saw in Jaskici on 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is the man.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could note a correct identification of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, when you were inside that house looking out and watching Dule Tadic beating the men, was your sister also in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she also looking out at the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall her saying anything to you as you both looked out of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember. I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did she say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She told us, "Look, Dule Tadic is killing all of the family, the husband, the father, the brother, everybody", and I said, "Yes".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the men had gone that day, did you then go outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without giving any names of anyone, did you see bodies in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the men that were taken away that day you have never seen again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your relatives were taken away as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of your relatives were taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bejdo Balic, Sefik Balic, Salko Jaskic, Munib Besic and Salih Softic and Ismet Jaskic, Hasan Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have efforts been ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have efforts been made, have you made efforts to find your relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the events that occurred in Jaskici did you leave Jaskici that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that Salih Softic was a relative of yours. Did you see him after the incident at Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left Jaskici, did you go to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you later put on a convoy and eventually went to Bosnian government territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujcic, to your knowledge on 14th June 1992 were your father or brother a member of any military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge on that date did they have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 10 o'clock tomorrow morning. (5.30 p.m.) (The court adjourned until the following day). 14
